Subject: EdgePilot private deployment — pricing breakdown request

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising for our on-prem inference use case. Procurement asked me to surface a couple of specifics so we can move the pilot forward:

1) How do you typically amortize the platform fee for a 6-month pilot versus a 36-month committed deployment? We need a clear view of capex vs opex for our finance team.
2) For an on-prem single-site deployment (4 nodes), what support tiers map to our internal SLA (4-hour response critical, 24x7)? Is Level 2 enough or do we need an SRE retainer?
3) If we agree to a usage floor (token or inference-hour minimum) in exchange for a lower platform fee, can you show the sensitivity (what thresholds move the invoice materially)?

Can you send a short worksheet we can drop into our procurement model and the SOW stub to share with our legal team?

Best,

Asha —

Thanks for the clear list. I looped in Marissa (commercial lead) and Naomi (solutions/onsite packaging). We put together a short sensitivity worksheet and a SOW stub — see attached. Key notes up front so you have the quick answers for procurement:

- Platform fee amortization: for pilots we typically offer pro-rata monthly for <12 months, or an option to convert the paid pilot fee toward a longer-term commitment (36 months) with a credit (typically 25-40% of pilot fee depending on commit size).
- Support tiers: Your described SLA (4-hour critical response, 24x7) is aligned to our "Priority SRE Retainer" band. Level 2 (standard enterprise) covers business-hours + extended coverage and on-call rotation; for guaranteed 4-hour critical response we recommend the retainer.
- Usage floor trade: we can provide a tiered matrix where lower platform fee is tied to a 12-month usage floor (tokens or inference-hours). The worksheet shows breakpoints at 25%, 50%, 75% of your expected run-rate — the material change in invoice occurs once you hit the 50% floor (we can move ~20% of platform fee into usage for high-variability customers).

I'm attaching: EdgePilot_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW stub) and PlatformFee_worksheet.xlsx (sensitivity model). We'll follow up with a short call to walk procurement/legal through the redlines.

Would Monday 10/5 10:00am PT work for a 30-min alignment?

Regards,

Asha / team —

Following Jordan's summary, a few practical clarifications from the commercial side:

• Pilot conversion credit: If KernLabs converts the 6-month pilot to a 36-month committed contract within 60 days of pilot completion, we apply a credit equal to 30% of all platform fees paid during the pilot toward your committed term.

• Example (worksheet snapshot): 6-month pilot platform fee = $240k (monthly $40k). If you commit to 36 months at an anchored usage profile, credit = $72k applied in month 1 of the committed term.

• Support placement: For your 4-node on-prem site we recommend the Priority SRE Retainer (monthly retainer + X hours included; overage at daily SRE rate). Level 2 covers incident triage and standard escalations but doesn't guarantee the 4-hour critical window. We can include a 2-week onboarding SRE block in the pilot at no extra fee to accelerate runbook handoff.

• Usage floor sensitivity: In the worksheet we included three scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive. With a 12-mo floor equal to 50% of expected usage, platform fee reduces by ~18% on year-one ARR; with 75% floor the reduction is ~28%. We can model token vs inference-hour floors — tell us which metric procurement prefers.

Next steps:
1) Confirm call Monday 10/5 10am PT — we'll bring legal and solutions engineering.
2) Tell us whether procurement wants token-based floors or inference-hour floors (we can convert metrics).
3) If okay, we'll send a redline-friendly SOW and a short commercial term sheet for your legal review.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

Marissa Cole
